sections.h2: The India-EU FTA was concluded a month before the war began

chart.title: The trade deal predates the war, so the sequence rules out a reaction to it
events: India-EU FTA concluded at the 16th India-EU Summit

sections.means: The FTA was concluded on 27 January 2026, a month before the war began on 28 February, so the sequence argues against a reaction.
sections.todo: Track freight costs on Gulf-linked lanes as the FTA phases in, since they can offset the tariff saving.

sections.h2: Hormuz and the Red Sea together disrupt an estimated 39% of global trade

chart.title: Compounded disruption reaches 39% of trade and 31% of shipments by September
chart.sub: Share of global total disrupted by September 2026, %.

sections.means: By September 2026 the disruption reached an estimated 39% of global trade and 31% of global shipments, at roughly $25bn in business cost.
sections.todo: Build more routes rather than rely on one chokepoint, as the Atlantic Council argues.

sections.h2: Red Sea rerouting already added 25-30% to Asia-Europe container rates

chart.title: The reroute premium predates the war; IMEC's 30% is a ceiling, not a result
chart.sub: Percent of freight cost. Ranges shown as bands.
chart.accent: Red Sea reroute premium, Asia-Europe container rates
rows: Red Sea reroute premium, Asia-Europe container rates

sections.means: The Red Sea reroute premium of 25-30% predates the 2026 war, and the 30% IMEC figure is a ceiling for a corridor still under construction.
sections.todo: Track the freight premium, not only the tariff cut, as the FTA phases in for India-Europe cargo.
